subject: Civil Engineering
title: The 2011 Tōhoku Earthquake and Tsunami
description: A micro-lesson that makes The 2011 Tōhoku Earthquake and Tsunami usable.

hook.text: March 11, 2011 — a magnitude 9.0 earthquake struck Japan. Then the ocean rose 130 feet.

buildup.text: Japan's buildings survived the shaking — decades of strict codes worked perfectly.

discovery.text: The tsunami overwhelmed seawalls designed for smaller waves — entire towns were swept away.

twist.text: The Fukushima nuclear plant's backup generators flooded — triggering a nuclear meltdown.

climax.text: 19,759 people died — nearly all from drowning, not building collapse.

punchline.text: Japan's buildings stood. The ocean didn't care. Some forces exceed all defenses.

quiz.question: What caused the Fukushima nuclear disaster during the 2011 earthquake?
options: The earthquake cracked the reactor containment vessel
The tsunami flooded backup generators, causing a loss of cooling and meltdown
Aftershocks shook the reactor beyond its design limits

details.summary: The 2011 Tohoku earthquake, magnitude 9.1, generated a devastating tsunami up to 40 meters high that overwhelmed coastal defenses in northeastern Japan, killing over 18,000 people and triggering the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
details.whyItMatters: Tohoku demonstrated that even the world's most prepared earthquake nation could be overwhelmed by events exceeding design assumptions. It reshaped global thinking about extreme event preparedness and nuclear safety.
takeaways: The tsunami reached heights of 40 meters, far exceeding seawall design heights
Japan's earthquake-resistant buildings performed excellently during the shaking
The Fukushima nuclear meltdown was triggered by tsunami flooding, not shaking

faq.question: Why did the tsunami exceed Japan's extensive coastal defense systems?
faq.answer: Japan's tsunami defenses were designed based on historical records going back centuries. The 2011 tsunami was generated by a magnitude 9.1 earthquake larger than hazard models predicted for this fault segment.

faq.question: How did the earthquake affect the Fukushima nuclear power plant?
faq.answer: The plant automatically shut down its reactors during the earthquake as designed. However, the subsequent tsunami overtopped the plant's seawall and flooded backup generators that powered cooling systems. Without cooling, three reactors suffered core meltdowns.
